title: Sports roundup: Kipchoge wants a marathon major in Kenya, Real Madrid hit PSV for five, Arsenal and City held
key_points: Eliud Kipchoge says Kenya should chase a World Marathon Major, at the launch of the new Sisibo Marathon in Eldoret.
The Sisibo Marathon on December 19 offers Ksh25 million in prizes, Ksh5 million for each winner, organisers say.
Champions League: Real Madrid beat PSV 5-1; Arsenal drew 1-1 with Dortmund; Man City drew 2-2 with Napoli.
Aston Villa lost 1-0 at Galatasaray. PSG play Roma on Wednesday.
content:
Here is the top sports news of the last two days, starting at home in Kenya.

Kipchoge: Kenya should host a marathon major

Marathon great Eliud Kipchoge says Kenya should aim to host one of the World Marathon Majors, the group of the biggest city marathons such as London, Berlin and New York. He spoke on Sunday at the launch of the new Sisibo Marathon in Eldoret, The Standard reported.

Kipchoge said he hopes the Sisibo race can become Africa's first World Marathon Major in 2027. That is his hope; no official bid decision has been reported. He also called for a Diamond League athletics meeting in Kenya. Athletics Kenya president Jackson Tuwei supported bringing more global events to Kenya and also spoke about the fight against doping.

Olympic 1500m champion Faith Kipyegon and New York City Marathon champion Sheila Chepkirui were among the stars at the launch.

Sisibo Marathon: big prize money

The first Sisibo Marathon will be run in Eldoret on December 19, 2026, according to Uasin Gishu News. Athletics Kenya official Barnaba Korir announced total prize money of Ksh25 million. The men's and women's winners will each get Ksh5 million, second place Ksh3 million and third place Ksh1 million. Organisers say it will be the richest race in Kenya and Africa, and that entry will be free and open to all.

Why it matters: Big races at home give Kenyan runners a chance to earn well without travelling abroad, and can bring visitors and money to the North Rift.

Champions League: Real Madrid strong, English clubs held

Tuesday night was matchday five of the Champions League league phase. Results, from AFP and France 24 reports:

  • Real Madrid 5-1 PSV Eindhoven: PSV led at half-time through an Ivan Perisic penalty. Madrid hit back with goals from Federico Valverde, Jude Bellingham, two from Kylian Mbappe and one from Vinicius Junior. Madrid have won all five games and have 15 points.
  • Arsenal 1-1 Borussia Dortmund: Viktor Gyokeres scored early for Arsenal, but Maximilian Beier levelled after the break.
  • Manchester City 2-2 Napoli: City came from behind twice. Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang scored for Napoli; Ayyoub Bouaddi and a late Rayan Cherki goal earned City a point.
  • Galatasaray 1-0 Aston Villa: a late Deniz Gul header beat Villa, who stay on nine points.
  • Other results: Como 1-0 AEK Athens, Slovan Bratislava 0-2 Real Betis, RB Leipzig 3-1 Lens, Bodo/Glimt 1-0 LASK.

On Wednesday, Paris Saint-Germain host Roma. A PSG win would take them level with Real Madrid on 15 points.

Coming up

In the Premier League this weekend, the big game is Arsenal against Manchester City on Sunday. At home, the row between Harambee Stars coach Benni McCarthy and the Football Kenya Federation over team preparations is still being watched closely by fans.
